I've got the picture. I can show you the picture of that band. Who's that? Sock? What did you say his name? Sock Horn. What did he play? Sax. Great, big, powerful man. Mm-hmm. I'm just not familiar with him. Where is he from?

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: See, William Manone with Roger. Roger Wolfe. Yeah. This is Roger Wolfe. He was with WDSU. He was a jockey, you see. A disc jockey. We were the first jazz band to ever play in the pops.

ctx.x: So you can get used to watching the machine. See if it's picking up. Testing. Yeah. You and Jim have voices that broadcast. Yeah well we got a bow bow on something. Which one? You were talking about Joe Gloriosa when the machine was off. Mmhmm. See the Flamingo Lounge 405 bourbon. Yeah. Bert Adam owned that. Bert Adam. It was Adam. A-D-A-M. They got B-E-R-T. A-D-A-M-S and it's and it was no S. No.

Who was Cecilia Kirsch? Cecilia Kirsch was a fine little singer and she was in love with a boy named Jock Robinson. Jock was playing with a very fine little band over on the Gulf Coast and she married Jock and they had I think four children. When Jock was on his way to St. Thomas Catholic Church in Long Beach when a drunk came along in a speeding automobile and hit him head on, hit his car head on and killed Jock. Killed Jock immediately. Toed him, just tore him all to pieces. The car was going some nearly a…

You know, I should remember this. Every Saturday morning we played on there. I should remember these Sunday concerts. It says, opening today, Sunday, September 4th, 1949. It's just about the time I came here. It was in the American Legion Crystal Room. 334. Well, that was on Royal Street, yes. But I really don't remember that. Back to corner of Conta. That may have been just before I got here.
